newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Feb 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Feb 12.

text.p: There are 139 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted, and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- EXPRESS NEWS said that although the Taiwanese government had stopped treating mainland hijackers as heros and was imprisoning them instead, the Chinese government had failed to communicate that fact to its people. As a result, some people in China still dreamed about becoming free souls in Taiwan if they hijacked a plane. It said the Chinese government should take measures to solve the problem.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD said the mainland government should not tolerate its border officials demanding money from Hong Kong truckers crossing the border. It said the problem reflected poor standards of discipline among security personnel at the border.

-- MING PAO said that crime in China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan was disturbing social order. Police in the four places had tried to join hands to crackdown on crime, but political differences undermined co-operation. It said the governments of the four places should put aside their differences and make joint efforts to eliminate triad forces.
